title: Add route/model/version context to cache telemetry (gateway + control-plane join keys)
creator: Ethan Park
content:
Problem
Cache metrics emitted by the runtime are only actionable if we can slice them the way we operate: by route, model, model version, deployment mode, and region. Today, runtime cache telemetry frequently lacks stable join keys, or uses inconsistent identifiers (e.g., route name vs route slug; model “alias” vs resolved model version). That prevents:
- Correct dashboard breakdowns (route/model/region)
- Debugging regressions after rollouts (version-mismatch misses)
- Recommendations MVP aggregation (per-route cache levers)

This ticket adds consistent route/model/version identifiers via gateway + control-plane context propagation, with strict allowlists to avoid metric cardinality blowups.

Goals / requirements
1) Consistent identifiers
- Route identifier must be stable across renames and match Console/analytics join keys.
- Model identifier must represent the resolved model (not user alias).
- Model version identifier must match control-plane rollout/version objects (the “pinned” or “resolved” version).

2) Joinability
- Cache telemetry must join with gateway request logs and Console analytics tables using the same keys.
- Keys must be consistent across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes.

3) Cardinality controls
- Do NOT emit free-form route names or customer-provided strings as metric labels.
- Provide an allowlist mechanism; everything else rolls up to “other/unknown”.

4) Backwards compatibility
- If context is missing (older gateways / private deployments), metrics should still emit with safe defaults (unknown/other) and a separate counter for missing context.

Non-goals
- Per-tenant identifiers as metric labels (out of scope; use tenant tier / deployment mode; tenant slicing happens in logs/analytics, not high-volume runtime metrics).

Implementation plan
A) Canonical keys (control-plane)
- Canonical route key: route_uid (stable opaque id)
- Canonical model key: model_uid (stable opaque id for catalog model)
- Canonical model version key: model_version_uid (stable opaque id used for rollouts)

B) Propagation path
- Gateway resolves request (route + resolved model version) and attaches context to runtime request metadata.
- Runtime picks up context and includes it in cache telemetry tags (with allowlists).

C) Metric label spec (as implemented)
- rw.route_uid: short, allowlisted stable id; else “other”
- rw.model_uid: allowlisted stable id; else “other”
- rw.model_version_uid: allowlisted stable id OR “other” (kept tighter than model_uid)
- rw.deployment_mode: hosted|dedicated|private
- rw.region: existing region label (already controlled)
- rw.cache_context: ok|missing|dropped_by_guard

Notes:
- We intentionally do not include route_name, model_name, customer route path, or prompt hashes as metric labels.
- “Allowlisted” means in-process map generated from control-plane config and updated via periodic refresh (no per-request lookups).

D) Cardinality / allowlist rules
- Default allowlist size targets (per region):
  - route_uid: top N=250 by request volume (rolling 7d)
  - model_uid: N=50
  - model_version_uid: N=200 (tightest; many versions can explode)
- Non-allowlisted values are rewritten to “other”.
- If gateway cannot provide the canonical uid, runtime sets rw.cache_context=missing.

E) Validation
- Staging: verify >99% of cache metrics have rw.cache_context=ok for Hosted routes on latest gateway.
- Compare joins:
  - Pick 10 routes and confirm route_uid in gateway logs == route_uid in runtime metrics.
  - Validate model_version_uid matches rollout event stream and Console model selector.
- Cardinality check:
  - Confirm series counts stay within Telemetry budget for cache metrics (via ingestion guard dashboards).

Acceptance criteria
- Cache telemetry can be filtered by route_uid, model_uid, model_version_uid, deployment_mode, and region in staging dashboards.
- Missing context counter is <1% on Hosted in prod after rollout (expected higher for Private until upgraded).
- No observed increase in dropped metric samples due to ingestion cardinality guards (or a documented, intentional rollup).
- No measurable gateway overhead (no extra control-plane RPC per request).

Rollout plan
1) Land gateway changes behind a feature flag: cache_telemetry_context_v1
2) Enable in staging + canary
3) Expand to 25% prod Hosted regions, monitor:
   - rw.cache_context=missing
   - cache metric series count
   - p95 gateway latency
4) Full rollout + communicate to SRE/Console teams that slicing is now reliable.

Links / related work
- Definitions/labels: ENG-4821
- Runtime uses this context: GitHub redwood PR-18426 (propagate route/model/version into runtime metrics)
- Cardinality controls: GitHub observability-pack PR-613
- Tagging notes: Drive doc “gateway-route-tagging-plan”
- Customer symptom motivating this: SUP-3912 (hit-rate dropped after model update; version-mismatch misses)

Decision log (key calls)
- Use stable uids (route_uid/model_uid/model_version_uid) rather than names to avoid rename churn.
- Allowlist + rollup to “other” is required; do not rely on ingestion-side dropping (too late / too expensive).
- Keep model_version_uid label tight; dashboards can usually pivot on model_uid and only drill into versions when allowlisted.

Open questions (resolved)
- Should we emit tenant_id? No (too high cardinality). We’ll rely on logs/analytics for tenant-level and keep metrics operational.
- Should we emit route_slug? No; slug changes and can be customer-derived in Private deployments.

Close-out summary
- Gateway now attaches canonical context for route/model/version (flagged), and runtime tags cache metrics accordingly with allowlists.
- Dashboards can slice cache hit-rate / wasted prefill by route/model/version in prod Hosted regions after rollout.
- Known limitation: Private deployments on older gateway versions will show rw.cache_context=missing until upgraded; tracked in follow-up ticket (not part of this sprint).
comments: 2025-03-05 (Amara Diallo): Drafted propagation contract: gateway -> runtime metadata includes route_uid, model_uid, model_version_uid, deployment_mode, region. Confirmed no per-request control-plane read; everything comes from route resolution path.

2025-03-06 (Nadia Rahman): Reviewed label proposal. Requested explicit rw.cache_context label to distinguish missing vs dropped-by-guard (helps telemetry QA). Approved stable uid approach; avoid route_name/model_name labels.
2025-03-07 (Caleb Johnson): Cardinality review: model_version_uid needs allowlist tighter than route_uid. Confirmed rollup to “other” in runtime (preferred) plus ingestion guards as backstop.
2025-03-10 (Logan Wright): Staging validation: >99.4% cache metrics have rw.cache_context=ok for Hosted. Found 0.6% missing due to older canary gateway pool; expected during rollout.
2025-03-12 (Allison Grant): Dashboard filters updated to use route_uid/model_uid/model_version_uid. Added panel showing rw.cache_context breakdown to catch regressions in tagging.
2025-03-14 (Connor O'Brien): Canary rollout complete (10% traffic). No gateway latency impact detected. Series count within budget; no unexpected ingestion drops.

2025-03-18 (Ethan Park): Marking Done. Full Hosted rollout completed in primary regions. Private upgrade guidance to be handled separately; SRE notified about expected rw.cache_context=missing in legacy Private clusters.
